government.note: On 1 January 2000 the Taliban's Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan held Kabul and about 90% of the country, ruled by its Supreme Leader (Amir al-Mu'minin) Mullah Mohammed Omar with a Council of Ministers; there was no legislature and no political parties were permitted. Only Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and the UAE recognised it; the UN seat was held by the rival Islamic State of Afghanistan (AFN). Stages since then: the Taliban lost Kabul on 13 November 2001; the Afghan Interim Administration under Hamid Karzai took office on 22 December 2001 (Bonn Agreement); the Emergency Loya Jirga elected Karzai head of the Transitional Islamic State on 13 June 2002 (in office 19 June 2002); the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan was established under the 2004 constitution, with a directly elected President and the National Assembly (Wolesi Jirga and Meshrano Jirga); and on 15 August 2021 the Taliban took Kabul and restored the Islamic Emirate, whose Supreme Leader is Hibatullah Akhundzada. Russia recognised the Islamic Emirate on 3 July 2025 (Reuters, cited by Wikipedia). The government type describes the situation in 2000; the 'constitution' flags are rough approximations.

holders.note: Head of state of the Islamic Emirate from the capture of Kabul. His followers had proclaimed him Amir al-Mu'minin on 4 April 1996 (Wikidata gives 3 April). He continued to lead the Taliban insurgency until his death on 23 April 2013.

holders.vacant_reason: The Islamic Emirate lost Kabul on 13 November 2001 and ceased to govern. The Taliban leaders (Mullah Omar until 2013, Akhtar Mansour 2013/2015-2016, Hibatullah Akhundzada from 2016) claimed the title during the insurgency; the state was headed by the Presidents of the Interim and Transitional Administrations and of the Islamic Republic (afg.president).

holders.note: Taliban leader since 25 May 2016; de facto head of state since the Taliban took Kabul on 15 August 2021.

holders.vacant_reason: Post abolished from the fall of Kabul on 13 November 2001 until 7 September 2021. The Islamic Republic had no Prime Minister; Abdullah Abdullah held the separate post of Chief Executive Officer from 29 September 2014 (Wikidata).

offices.note: Before 22 December 2001 the presidency was held by Burhanuddin Rabbani of the rival Islamic State of Afghanistan (afn.president). The two-term limit is that of the 2004 constitution, which the government's notes do not otherwise model.

offices.review_note: The five-year term and two-term limit come from the 2004 constitution as summarised in the 2014 election article ('not eligible to run due to term limits'); the term length itself was not read from a fetched source. Confirm both.

system.note: The chamber did not exist on 1 January 2000: the Taliban's Islamic Emirate had no legislature. It was created by the 2004 constitution, first elected in 2005 (249 seats; 250 from 2018), and stopped functioning after 15 August 2021. All seats are therefore recorded as vacant for 2000. Members were elected by single non-transferable vote in provincial constituencies, mostly as independents without party lists. The 102-member Meshrano Jirga (upper house) was chosen indirectly and by appointment and is not modelled.

no_parties_reason: The Taliban's Islamic Emirate permitted no political parties in 2000. The Taliban themselves are a movement rather than a party; they are recorded as afg.taliban so that their leaders can be referenced. Parties registered under the Islamic Republic (2004-2021) are recorded as not yet founded, or cross-referenced from AFN for the United Front parties.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Estimate only: no national vote had been held since the 1980s. The split reflects 2000 conditions in Taliban-held territory: the Taliban movement (islamist), Pashtun tribal structures and local notables (tribal_traditional), ethnic regional parties surviving outside the front line (regionalist), moderate Islamic politics later represented by the Bonn process (islamic_democrat), supporters of the exiled former king Zahir Shah's Rome process (constitutional_monarchist), the professional and returnee class (technocratic) and former PDPA supporters (reformed_communist).

civil_war.note: Afghan Civil War (1996-2001): on 1 January 2000 the Taliban's Islamic Emirate was fighting the United Front (Northern Alliance) forces of the Islamic State of Afghanistan in the north-east.

claims.note: The Islamic Emirate claimed all of Afghanistan, including the north-eastern territory held by the Islamic State of Afghanistan (United Front).
